gen_risks.description: Recurrent climate-related shocks such as severe droughts and rainfall volatility threaten rural livelihoods and economic stability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize adaptive Social Registry and National Population Registry systems to rapidly identify affected households and deliver targeted shock-responsive assistance.
gen_risks.evidence: climate-related shocks, primarily droughts, represent significant risks to the Moroccan economy.

gen_risks.description: Informal sector workers may resist enrolling in the National Population Registry due to fears of tax exposure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct targeted outreach campaigns clarifying data protection safeguards and emphasizing social protection benefits.
gen_risks.evidence: workers in the informal sector, are wary of providing their information to the government due to perceived risks of making them susceptible to taxation.

gen_risks.description: Non-salaried workers experience income cyclicality, leading to high default rates on mandatory health insurance contributions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate dynamic welfare evaluation tools in the Social Registry to maintain social protection coverage during income disruptions.
gen_risks.evidence: less than 15 percent of non-salaried workers are paying their contribution and benefit from coverage against health-related risks.

gen_risks.description: Vulnerable, disabled, or geographically isolated individuals risk exclusion from registration due to communication or physical accessibility barriers.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy mobile units, satellite communication technology, and local Citizen Service Centers alongside an inclusive Stakeholder Engagement Plan.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential negative social impacts from project activities are mainly related to the exclusion of some vulnerable groups due to inefficient or inadequate public communication

gen_risks.description: Processing extensive biographic and biometric personal data creates potential data privacy, security, and unauthorized disclosure risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply privacy-by-design principles, enforce strict compliance with national Law 09-08, and provide data security training for system operators.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential negative social impacts from project activities are mainly related to... data protection issues.

gen_risks.description: Capacity constraints within the Ministry of Interior may delay operationalizing the National Registry Agency and transferring operational management.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated institutional capacity building, recruit key technical leadership, and execute formal transition operational manuals.
gen_risks.evidence: This rapid expansion has strained the government’s and the MoI’s capacity to take steps in operationalizing the NRA.

gen_risks.description: Social protection intake and benefit targeting processes may be vulnerable to system error, fraud, and corruption.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and deploy an end-to-end error, fraud, and corruption monitoring system integrated with biometric deduplication and database cross-checks.
gen_risks.evidence: design and develop an end-to-end Error, Fraud, and Corruption (EFC) monitoring system and EFC mitigation strategy

gen_risks.description: Deployment and maintenance of electronic hardware and mobile equipment across regions may lead to improper e-waste disposal.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement formal e-waste management procedures in compliance with Ministry of Interior asset disposal protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: Risks associated with the use of electronic devices (such as mobile units) include the potential generation of e-waste and its improper disposal.

gen_risks.description: Reliance on spreadsheets and manual national budget software data extraction may introduce quality and timeliness issues in financial reporting.
gen_risks.mitigation: Procure and operationalize customized accounting software to automate project financial reporting and IFR generation.
gen_risks.evidence: the use of a spreadsheet “Excel” and data extracted from the national budget execution software may lead to some challenges

gen_risks.description: Using shared budget lines across multiple World Bank financed projects risks duplicate claiming of Eligible Expenditure Program costs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish distinct, dedicated budget sub-codes within the Ministry of Interior budget for all performance-based condition activities.
gen_risks.evidence: risk of duplication or overlap due to the use of the same budget line “AMO-TADAMON” to justify expenditure... on programs already financed

gen_risks.description: Flaws in the Proxy-Means Test scoring formula may generate high targeting error rates, causing inclusion and exclusion errors.
gen_risks.mitigation: Re-evaluate and update the intake questionnaire and scoring formula using empirical household expenditure survey data.
gen_risks.evidence: develop a strategy to reduce potential exclusion and inclusion errors

gen_risks.description: Infrastructure and network deficits across remote Civil Registry Offices (BECs) may hamper real-time birth and death data exchange with the NPR.
gen_risks.mitigation: Upgrade IT hardware, software, and connectivity across all 2,200 local Civil Registry Offices nationwide.
gen_risks.evidence: all the 2,200 Civil Registry Offices (Bureau d’Etat Civil, BEC) nationwide, some of which are in very isolated areas and require substantial investments

gt_risks.description: Stakeholder risk is assessed as Substantial. Given the complex nature of the operation and the involvement of multiple stakeholders in the implementation of the National Population Register (NPR) and the Social Registry (SR), the Project Management Unit (PMU) will need to put considerable effort into ensuring better coordination to achieve the PDO. The national rollout and the improvement of the NPR and the SR will need strong stakeholder engagement, including citizens concerned by social protection programs who are often poor and vulnerable.
gt_risks.mitigation: The communication strategy will continue to inform all stakeholders involved in project implementation and will capitalize on lessons learned from the first Identity and Targeting for Social Protection project (P155198). The PMU envisions improving the grievance mechanism at local and national levels and establishing a system to promote citizen engagement and transparency. The Inter-Ministerial Steering Committee is responsible for developing guidelines for the strategic policy for the envisaged reform and ensuring a link with the ongoing social protection reform. Technical work will also cover a process evaluation to identify challenges, propose remedies, and provide recommendations to enhance system implementation at central and local levels.
